notice: FULLY SYNTHETIC AND ILLUSTRATIVE. Every measurement was invented for documentation; this is not an NHANES participant and not part of the PhysioBench v0.1.0 ten-item benchmark. It is excluded from item_specs.yaml, items.jsonl, the case mapping and the answer key.
prompt_format: Same template, rules, neutral question and response schema as the benchmark's bronchodilator-response items (benchmark/prompt_template.txt; src/build_items.py, family 'bdr').

case_data_notes.invented: Age, sex, height, pre/post FEV1 and FVC, quality grades and exam status were invented. Volumes are whole mL.
case_data_notes.derived: fev1fvc_pre_ratio = 2040 mL / 3010 mL, as computed by src/bdr.py. GLI Global 2022 race-neutral predicted FEV1, predicted FVC and FEV1/FVC LLN computed for a 44-year-old female, 1.630 m, with rspiro 0.5 (pred_GLIgl, LLN_GLIgl) under R 4.5.2, the functions used by src/gli_reference.R.
case_data_notes.quality_grades: A = exceeds ATS standards (NHANES grading scale).

reference_answer.physiological_explanation: FEV1 rose by 500 mL, 24.5% of its pre-bronchodilator value, and FVC rose by 460 mL, 15.3% of its pre-bronchodilator value; each measurement independently meets both GINA 2026 criteria (>=12% and >=200 mL in the same measurement), so GINA is positive. Relative to GLI predicted values, the FEV1 change is 17.9% and the FVC change 13.6% of predicted; both exceed the ERS/ATS 2022 criterion of >10% of predicted, so ERS/ATS is positive. The guidelines use different denominators (pre-bronchodilator value vs predicted value) but agree here because both changes are well clear of every threshold; the smallest margin is FVC, 3.3 percentage points above 12% of baseline and 3.6 points above 10% of predicted. A rise in both FEV1 and FVC is consistent with bronchodilator-reversible airflow limitation, possibly with reduced air trapping.
reference_answer.limitations: A positive bronchodilator response is a physiological finding, not a diagnosis: it supports reversible airflow limitation but does not by itself establish asthma, and it can occur in COPD. The baseline FEV1/FVC (0.678) is below 0.70 and below the GLI LLN, but whether obstruction persists after the bronchodilator was not asked and needs post-bronchodilator interpretation and clinical context. This is a single test session; responses vary between occasions, and interpretation depends on repeatability, symptoms and history. Age is recorded in whole years, which slightly affects the predicted values.

reference_details.source: Computed by src/bdr.py (via build_items.recompute) and checked independently with exact rational arithmetic; verified by tests/test_examples.py.
